log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Light Screen ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar. Lead Gengar+Klefki: Klefki sets Prankster Reflect/LightScreen turn 1 while Gengar Mega Evolves into Shadow Tag at 200 Spe, trapping and threatening with Dazzling Gleam vs Garchomp or Shadow Ball vs trapped Rotom-W. Back Gyarados provides Intimidate+Waterfall for Garchomp/Blaziken/Arcanine and DD sweep potential; Aegislash adds Wide Guard for RockSlide/EQ spread, Close Combat for Tinkaton/Archaludon, and King's Shield safety. Ditto stays in reserve—Blaziken sash is handled by Gyarado
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar @ Gengarite confirmed 200 Spe / 222 SpA / 137 HP / 100 Def / 115 SpD. Scarf Rotom-Wash (~226 Spe) outspeeds Mega Gengar and is immune to Thunder Wave (Electric-type immunity). Shadow Tag still traps it. Dazzling Gleam spread vs Garchomp = 27-69.4% (2HKO chunk). Shadow Ball vs Rotom-W = 28.7-92% neutral. Focus Blast vs Archaludon = possible OHKO but 70% acc. Opponent roster: Garchomp ExpertBelt Jolly 134-169, Arcanine Leftovers Adamant Intimidate 115-147, Tinkaton Sitrus Careful MoldBreaker 114-146, Rotom-W Scarf Timid 116-151 (226 max with Scarf), Archaludon LifeOrb Modest Sturdy 105-137, Blaziken FocusSash Jolly SpeedBoost 110-145 (+1 = 165-217). Key plan: Klefki Prankster screens mitigate damage, TWave slows non-Electric threats (Garchomp, Blaziken, Arcanine, Tinkaton). Gyarados Waterfall SE vs Blaziken/Garchomp/Arcanine breaks sash. Aegislash immune to Fighting (Blaziken CC), resists Dragon (Garchomp), Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide/EQ spread. Ditto Scarf in reserve for emergency revenge if Blaziken gets +2.

decisions.rationale: Lead Tinkaton/Archaludon to immediately check Mega Gengar; Archaludon's LO Dark Pulse OHKOes, Tinkaton resists both STABs and chips with Knock Off. Back Garchomp/Arcanine handle Aegislash/Klefki with Ground/Fire coverage and Intimidate to blunt Gyarados. Rotom-Wash and Blaziken saved for late-game pivot and cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag), Klefki (Prankster screens/TWave), Gyarados (Intimidate/Dragon Dance), Aegislash (Stance Change/Wide Guard), Rotom-Heat, Ditto (Choice Scarf Imposter). Plan: Tinkaton/Archaludon lead to check Mega Gengar turn 1; Garchomp/Arcanine back for Aegislash/Klefki and Intimidate support; Rotom-Wash pivot and Blaziken cleanup for late game. Ditto will Transform into whichever is faster/facing it; be ready to play around Imposter by not revealing Blaziken's Speed Boost too early.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Gengar)
decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve for Shadow Tag + 200 Spe outspeeding all. Focus Blast is only meaningful damage option (80-189% vs Archaludon, possible OHKO). Light Screen from Prankster Klefki goes up first, halving Dark Pulse (40-90% -> 20-45%) so Gengar survives even if Focus Blast misses. If Focus Blast KOs Archaludon, Gengar easily tanks Knock Off. Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb are NVE/immune vs both foes.

Scarf Rotom-Wash (~226 Spe) outspeeds Mega Gengar and is immune to Thunder Wave (Electric-type immunity). Shadow Tag still traps it. Dazzling Gleam spread vs Garchomp = 27-69.4% (2HKO chunk). Shadow Ball vs Rotom-W = 28.7-92% neutral. Focus Blast vs Archaludon = 80.2-189.1% possible OHKO but 70% acc. Knock Off Tinkaton vs Mega Gengar = 20.4-60.7%. Dark Pulse Archaludon vs Mega Gengar = 40.7-90.4%. Light Screen halves Dark Pulse to ~20-45%. Opponent roster: Garchomp ExpertBelt Jolly 134-169, Arcanine Leftovers Adamant Intimidate 115-147, Tinkaton Sitrus Careful MoldBreaker 114-146, Rotom-W Scarf Timid 116-151 (226 max with Scarf), Archaludon LifeOrb Modest Sturdy 105-137, Blaziken FocusSash Jolly SpeedBoost 110-145 (+1 = 165-217). Key plan: Klefki Prankster screens mitigate damage, TWave slows non-Electric threats (Garchomp, Blaziken, Arcanine, Tinkaton). Gyarados Waterfall SE vs Blaziken/Garchomp/Arcanine breaks sash. Aegislash immune to Fighting (Blaziken CC), resists Dragon (Garchomp), Wide Guard blocks Rock Slide/EQ spread. Ditto Scarf in reserve for emergency revenge if Blaziken gets +2.

decisions.rationale: Aegislash resists Tinkaton's Play Rough (0.5x), Close Combat hits both foes SE, and King's Shield protects on entry. Gyarados is 4x weak to Archaludon Thunderbolt — instant KO risk. Light Screen already halves Dark Pulse damage to Aegislash. Gyarados saved for when Archaludon is removed.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar fainted turn 1 to Knock Off+Dark Pulse after Focus Blast missed Archaludon. Light Screen 8 turns remaining. Aegislash brought in as Gengar replacement: resists Play Rough, Close Combat SE vs both Tinkaton and Archaludon, King's Shield for scouting. Gyarados preserved in back — 4x Thunderbolt weak, must wait until Archaludon removed. Klefki Prankster screens + TWave support ongoing. Opponent: Tinkaton Sitrus Careful MoldBreaker 114-146 Spe, Archaludon LifeOrb Modest Sturdy 105-137 Spe at 90% HP. Key wincon: Aegislash Close Combat pressure + Klefki TWave on faster threats, Gyarados cleanup late.

decisions.rationale: Gengar must be removed turn 1 to avoid Shadow Tag lock. Archaludon's Life Orb Dark Pulse + Tinkaton's Knock Off are both super-effective and should KO Gengar before it Mega Evolves and moves. Even if Klefki paralyzes one, we eliminate the primary threat. Protect lines concede too much initiative to Prankster screens.
decisions.notebook: Opponent lead: Gengar (Gengarite, Timid, Cursed Body) + Klefki (Light Clay, Bold, Prankster). Back: Gyarados (Jolly, Life Orb, Intimidate), Aegislash (Brave, Leftovers, Stance Change, Wide Guard), Rotom-Heat (Timid, Expert Belt, Levitate), Ditto (Jolly, Choice Scarf, Imposter). Plan: Tinkaton/Archaludon lead to check Mega Gengar turn 1; Garchomp/Arcanine back for Aegislash/Klefki and Intimidate support. Ditto transforms into faster/facing Pokémon; avoid revealing Blaziken's Speed Boost early. Game 1: opponent leads Gengar+Klefki; going for turn 1 KO on Gengar with double super-effective Dark Pulse + Knock Off.

decisions.rationale: King's Shield keeps Aegislash in Shield Forme (160 Def/162 SpD), blocks Tinkaton's contact Knock Off and drops its Attack. Prankster TWave (priority +1) paralyzes Tinkaton before it moves, dropping it to 57-73 Spe (below Aegislash 72). Light Screen halves Archaludon's Dark Pulse. Next turn both foes are weakened: Tinkaton para+Atk-lowered, Aegislash free to Close Combat Archaludon safely. TWave Tinkaton over Archaludon because Tinkaton's physical Knock Off bypasses Light Screen and it's the fast
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opponent leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (Life Orb, Modest, Sturdy, 105-137 Spe, 90% HP). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak, keep hidden until Archaludon removed. Light Screen active. Wincon: Aegislash CC pressure on Steels, Klefki TWave speed control, Gyarados late cleanup. Watch for Garchomp EQ (2x vs Aegislash) and Rotom-W Volt Switch.

decisions.rationale: Double targeting Aegislash with super-effective Knock Off and Dark Pulse deals significant damage (42-91%) before they can set up Reflect. Archaludon's Dark Pulse is non-contact, so it safely bypasses King's Shield's Attack drop. Tinkaton risks an Attack drop if Aegislash uses King's Shield, but we can switch it out later if needed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar+Klefki, back includes Aegislash, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat, Ditto. Light Screen is up for 7 turns, halving our special damage. Aegislash has King's Shield, Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Ball. Klefki has Prankster, Light Screen, Reflect, Thunder Wave, Dazzling Gleam. Archaludon's Dark Pulse is non-contact, bypassing King's Shield's Attack drop. Tinkaton's Knock Off is physical, not halved by Light Screen, but triggers King's Shield's Attack drop. Plan: Damage Aegislash heavily turn 2. Switch Tinkaton out if Attack drops. Bring in Arcanine/Garchomp for Intimidate/Rough Skin support against physical threats. Ditto transforms into faster/facing Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Klefki Prankster TWave hits Archaludon first (90% acc, 25% full para chance). Aegislash is slowest so it tanks both incoming hits in Shield forme (Def160/SpD162 + Light Screen): Dark Pulse ~15-26% with screen, Knock Off ~9-29% with atk-1. Combined ~55% max — survives comfortably. Then Blade Aegislash Close Combat does 37-78% to Archaludon (2x SE). Paralyzed Archaludon (52-68 Spe) drops below Aegislash (72) next turn for easy cleanup. Wincon stays on track.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opponent leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (Life Orb, Modest, Sturdy, 105-137 Spe). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak, keep hidden until Archaludon removed. Light Screen active. Tinkaton atk -1 from King's Shield. Wincon: Aegislash CC pressure on Steels, Klefki TWave speed control, Gyarados late cleanup. Watch for Garchomp EQ (2x vs Aegislash and Klefki) and Rotom-W Volt Switch. Archaludon paralyzed T3 if TWave hits — Aegislash outspeeds next turn.

decisions.rationale: Thunder Wave on Klefki (90% acc) neutralizes Prankster paralysis/screens threat. Dark Pulse is non-contact super-effective vs Aegislash, bypassing King's Shield's Atk drop. Tinkaton stays useful at -1 rather than risking -3. Safest path to progress both matchups.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar+Klefki, back: Aegislash, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat, Ditto. Light Screen (opponent side) halves our special damage. Aegislash: King's Shield (drops Atk 2 on contact), Wide Guard, Close Combat (2x Archaludon), Shadow Ball (0.5x Archaludon, 0.25x Tinkaton). Klefki: Prankster, Light Clay, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Dazzling Gleam. Archaludon Dark Pulse non-contact, safe vs King's Shield. Tinkaton Knock Off physical, triggers King's Shield drop. Plan: Paralyze Klefki, damage Aegislash with Dark Pulse. Switch Tinkaton if Atk drops further. Bring Arcanine/Garchomp for Intimidate/Rough Skin vs physical threats. Ditto transforms into faster Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 8% is guaranteed to move before para-Aegi (105-137 vs 36). King's Shield (+4 priority) blocks all incoming attacks and reverts Aegi to Shield forme (150/162 defenses). Klefki Dazzling Gleam does 12.2%+ min to Archaludon—KO at 8% if it doesn't Protect. If Arch Protects, Aegi is still safe in Shield forme for next turn. Light Screen halves Dark Pulse so Aegi survives at 62%. Best risk-reward: safe reset plus potential KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (Life Orb, Modest, Sturdy, 105-137 Spe). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak, keep hidden until Archaludon removed. Light Screen active. Tinkaton atk -1 from King's Shield. Wincon: Aegislash CC pressure on Steels, Klefki TWave speed control, Gyarados late cleanup. Watch for Garchomp EQ (2x vs Aegislash and Klefki) and Rotom-W Volt Switch. Klefki TWave missed Archaludon twice (T2, T3) — 90% acc, unlucky. Aegislash is Brave nature (slow, mixed attacker). King's Shield resets to Shield forme (Def 150/SpD 162).

decisions.rationale: Protect keeps Tinkaton safe from King's Shield drop and Klefki Thunder Wave. Archaludon Dark Pulse is non-contact (safe from King's Shield drop) and should KO Aegislash from 62% HP even with Light Screen (81-212% range). If Aegislash uses Close Combat, Sturdy saves Archaludon at 1 HP and Dark Pulse still KOs. Removes major threat while preserving options.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar+Klefki, back: Aegislash, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat, Ditto. Light Screen halves special damage. Aegislash: King's Shield (drops Atk 2 on contact), Wide Guard, Close Combat (2x Archaludon), Shadow Ball. Klefki: Prankster, Light Clay, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Dazzling Gleam. Archaludon Dark Pulse non-contact, safe vs King's Shield. Tinkaton Knock Off physical, triggers King's Shield drop. Plan: Paralyze Klefki, damage Aegislash with Dark Pulse. Switch Tinkaton if Atk drops further. Bring Arcanine/Garchomp for Intimidate/Rough Skin vs physical threats. Ditto transforms into faster Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp's 169 Speed outspeeds both paralyzed Aegislash (36-50) and Klefki (95-127). Earthquake hits Klefki SE and Aegislash neutrally, pressuring both. Rough Skin punishes Aegislash's Close Combat. Arcanine is slower and Flare Blitz is NVE vs Aegislash; Intimidate less valuable since Aegislash already at -1 Atk.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar+Klefki, back: Aegislash, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat, Ditto. Light Screen halves special damage (5 turns). Aegislash: King's Shield (drops Atk 2 on contact), Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Ball; at -1 Def/-1 SpD when in Blade forme. Klefki: Prankster, Light Clay, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Dazzling Gleam. Archaludon Dark Pulse non-contact, safe vs King's Shield. Tinkaton Knock Off physical, triggers King's Shield drop. Plan: Paralyze Klefki, damage Aegislash with Dark Pulse. Switch Tinkaton if Atk drops further. Bring Arcanine/Garchomp for Intimidate/Rough Skin vs physical threats. Ditto transforms into faster Pokémon. Garchomp brings Earthquake spread pressure and Rough Skin chip. Arcanine provides Intimidate and Flare Blitz for Klefki.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Klefki)
decisions.rationale: Wide Guard (pri+3) blocks Garchomp EQ/Rock Slide for both mons — EQ would KO Aegislash and possibly Klefki with Expert Belt. Klefki Prankster TWave on Garchomp (90% acc) gives speed control: paralyzed Garchomp (67-84 Spe) drops below Klefki 95. Aegislash stays Shield forme (high Def). Worst case if no spread move: Tinkaton Knock Off 21-34% on Aegislash, survivable. Next turn: freed to attack with Garchomp slowed.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (Life Orb, Modest, Sturdy, 105-137 Spe). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak, keep hidden until Archaludon removed. Archaludon fainted T4. Light Screen active. Tinkaton atk -1 from King's Shield. Wincon: Aegislash CC pressure on Steels, Klefki TWave speed control, Gyarados late cleanup. Klefki TWave missed twice (T2 Tinkaton, T3 Archaludon) — 90% acc, unlucky. Aegislash Brave (slow, mixed). Garchomp EQ is 2x vs both Aegislash and Klefki — Wide Guard blocks it. Expert Belt boosts Garchomp SE hits 1.2x. Watch Rotom-W Volt Switch and Scarf speed tier.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Garchomp Earthquake hits both foes for 2x damage, pressuring -1 Def Aegislash and Klefki. Tinkaton Protect avoids King's Shield's -2 Atk drop on contact, critical since Tinkaton is already at -1 Atk. Though Protect success is reduced, it's safer than risking further Attack loss. This maximizes damage while protecting Tinkaton's offensive presence.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Gengar+Klefki, back: Aegislash, Gyarados, Rotom-Heat, Ditto. Light Screen halves special damage (5 turns). Aegislash: King's Shield (drops Atk 2 on contact), Wide Guard, Close Combat, Shadow Ball; at -1 Def/-1 SpD when in Blade forme, paralyzed. Klefki: Prankster, Light Clay, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Dazzling Gleam; immune to Electric. Archaludon Dark Pulse non-contact, safe vs King's Shield. Tinkaton Knock Off physical, triggers King's Shield drop. Plan: Paralyze Klefki (but it's Steel-type, immune to T-Wave), damage Aegislash with Earthquake. Switch Tinkaton if Atk drops further. Bring Arcanine/Garchomp for Intimidate/Rough Skin vs physical threats. Ditto transforms into faster Pokémon. Garchomp brings Earthquake spread pressure and Rough Skin chip. Arcanine provides Intimidate and Flare Blitz for Klefki.

decisions.rationale: Switch Aegislash to Gyarados for Intimidate (both foes -1 Atk) and permanent Ground immunity, solving the EQ problem that forced Wide Guard every turn. Klefki Reflect (Prankster priority, up before foes move) + existing Light Screen gives full screen coverage. Garchomp EQ vs Klefki drops to ~18-32% with Intimidate+Reflect. Tinkaton Knock Off vs Gyarados is negligible at -2 Atk. Next turn: TWave Tinkaton behind screens + Gyarados DD to start sweep.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (fainted T4). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak to Rotom-W. Klefki TWave missed twice T2/T3 (90% acc, unlucky). Tinkaton favors Knock Off, uses Protect frequently (streak 2 by T5). Garchomp favors Earthquake. Wincon: Gyarados DD sweep behind screens with Klefki TWave speed control. Watch Rotom-W Scarf speed tier (116-151) as Gyarados counter — Gyarados at +1 Spe (219) outspeeds. Aegislash Brave (slow, mixed, para).

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Tinkaton Protect avoids King's Shield Atk drop; Garchomp Earthquake hits both paralyzed Aegislash (-1 Def) and Klefki for 2x, aiming to KO or heavily damage both. Even if Protect fails, Tinkaton's Sitrus Berry provides recovery. Garchomp's Rough Skin chips physical attackers.
decisions.notebook: Opponent back: Gyarados (Water/Flying, Intimidate, LifeOrb, DragonDance threat), Rotom-Heat (Electric/Fire, Levitate, ExpertBelt), Ditto (Imposter, ChoiceScarf, transforms). Light Screen 3 turns. Aegislash King's Shield drops Atk 2 on contact; Klefki Prankster, immune to T-Wave. Plan: Earthquake spread pressure, Protect from King's Shield, Arcanine Intimidate vs physical, watch Ditto transform.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Opp has only 2 Pokemon left. DDance resets Gyarados to neutral Atk (177) and 219 Spe, outspeeding everything. Next turn Waterfall does 73-167% to Arcanine (likely OHKO). All foe attacks on Gyarados are negligible: EQ immune, Rock Slide/Dragon Claw halved by Reflect and weakened by Garchomp -1 Atk. Klefki TWave (Prankster) para-locks Arcanine permanently. Even if Klefki falls to Flare Blitz, Gyarados at +1 sweeps both remaining foes alone with Aegislash in back.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (fainted T4). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak to Rotom-W. Klefki TWave missed twice T2/T3 (90% acc, unlucky). Tinkaton favors Knock Off, uses Protect frequently (streak 2 by T5). Garchomp favors Earthquake. Opp likes Protect reads. Wincon: Gyarados DD sweep behind screens with Klefki TWave speed control. Watch Rotom-W Scarf speed tier (116-151) as Gyarados counter — Gyarados at +1 Spe (219) outspeeds. Aegislash Brave (slow, mixed, para). Gyarados Waterfall at neutral Atk does 73-167% to Arcanine (likely OHKO); at -1 Atk only 49-112%. Reflect halves all incoming physical damage to my side.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados is the win condition if it Dragon Dances behind Reflect. Will-O-Wisp burns it, neutering physical attacks even after setup. Rock Slide pressures Gyarados (2x, 1x after Reflect) and Klefki (0.5x, 0.25x after Reflect). Klefki likely Thunder Waves Garchomp via Prankster, but burning Gyarados is the priority. Even paralyzed, Garchomp can follow up next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent back: Rotom-Heat (Electric/Fire, Levitate, ExpertBelt), Ditto (Imposter, ChoiceScarf). Klefki Prankster, Light Clay, immune to T-Wave (Steel type). Aegislash paralyzed 74% HP, King's Shield drops Atk 2 on contact. Gyarados LifeOrb Intimidate Jolly, Dragon Dance threat. Screens: Light Screen 2 turns, Reflect 7 turns. Plan: Burn Gyarados to prevent sweep, pressure Klefki with super-effective moves, watch for Ditto transform. Arcanine Intimidate vs physical threats. Garchomp Earthquake spread pressure, Rock Slide for Gyarados.

decisions.rationale: Opp has only 2 Pokemon left. Gyarados outspeeds and chunks Arcanine with SE Waterfall before it can Flare Blitz Klefki. Klefki Dazzling Gleam chips Garchomp SE (~21-48%). Reflect + Garchomp -1 Atk makes Rock Slide only ~13-16% on Gyarados. Even if Klefki falls to Flare Blitz, both foes are in KO range next turn with Aegislash in back. Light Screen irrelevant since both foes are physical.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp leads Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe) + Archaludon (fainted T4). Back: Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe), Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, 146 Spe, Intimidate) — 4x Tbolt weak to Rotom-W. Klefki TWave missed twice T2/T3 (90% acc, unlucky). Tinkaton favors Knock Off, uses Protect frequently (streak 2 by T5). Garchomp favors Earthquake. Opp likes Protect reads. Wincon: Gyarados DD sweep behind screens with Klefki TWave speed control. Watch Rotom-W Scarf speed tier (116-151) as Gyarados counter — Gyarados at +1 Spe (219) outspeeds. Aegislash Brave (slow, mixed, para). Gyarados Waterfall at neutral Atk does 73-167% to Arcanine (likely OHKO); at -1 Atk only 49-112%. Reflect halves all incoming physical damage to my side. Opp only has Garchomp + Arcanine remaining in game 1 (Tinkaton + Archaludon fainted). Gyarados burned T7 — physical damage halved, needs +2 Atk to fully offset burn. Light Screen irrelevant vs current physical-only opponent.

decisions.rationale: Klefki at 54% is the priority target. Flare Blitz + Earthquake are both super-effective into Klefki; even with Reflect and Garchomp's -1 Atk, Expert Belt Earthquake plus Adamant Flare Blitz should KO or leave it at 1HP, removing Prankster Thunder Wave threat. Arcanine survives Gyarados Waterfall behind Reflect, and Gyarados is burned so its physical output is halved. Light Screen fades after this turn, so we must act now before Klefki paralyzes both our mons.
decisions.notebook: Opponent back: Rotom-Heat (Electric/Fire, Levitate, ExpertBelt), Ditto (Imposter, ChoiceScarf). Klefki Prankster, Light Clay, immune to T-Wave (Steel type). Aegislash paralyzed 74% HP, King's Shield drops Atk 2 on contact. Gyarados LifeOrb Intimidate Jolly, Dragon Dance threat, now burned. Screens: Light Screen fades turn 8, Reflect 6 turns left. Plan: Burn Gyarados to prevent sweep, pressure Klefki with super-effective moves, watch for Ditto transform. Arcanine Intimidate vs physical threats. Garchomp Earthquake spread pressure, Rock Slide for Gyarados. If Klefki falls, Gyarados becomes manageable with burn + Arcanine Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is the last foe at 44%. Gyarados outspeeds (219 vs 134-169) and Waterfall (burned, ~12-25%) plus Klefki Dazzling Gleam (SE, ~28-63% single-target) totals 40-88%, KOing in most lines. If Garchomp Protects, no harm done — retry next turn. If EQ KOs Klefki, Gyarados still wins the 1v1 since Garchomp can't meaningfully damage it through Reflect + -1 Atk. No risk to Gyarados this turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Mega Gengar fainted T1 (Focus Blast missed). Opp brought Garchomp (Expert Belt, Jolly, 134-169 Spe), Arcanine (Leftovers, Adamant, Intimidate, 115-147 Spe, fainted T8), Tinkaton (Sitrus, Careful, Mold Breaker, 114-146 Spe, fainted T6), Archaludon (Life Orb, Modest, Sturdy, 105-137 Spe, fainted T4). Back: Rotom-W (Scarf, Timid, 116-151 Spe), Blaziken (Sash, Jolly, Speed Boost, 110-145 Spe). My back: Aegislash (Leftovers, Brave, 72 Spe, para, mixed, Wide Guard/Close Combat/Shadow Ball/King's Shield). Gyarados burned T7 — physical damage halved, needs +2 Atk to fully offset. Klefki TWave missed twice T2/T3 (90% acc). Opp likes Protect reads; Garchomp favors Earthquake. Wincon: Gyarados DD sweep behind screens; Gyarados at +1 Spe (219) outspeeds all opp mons including Scarf Rotom-W (116-151). Watch Rotom-W Scarf as Gyarados counter in games 2-3. Aegislash Brave is slow mixed, para limits it. Opp Protect frequency high — consider double-attack lines to punish Protect stalls.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Earthquake guarantees KO on Klefki (81.7-186.4% into 14% HP), removing the Dazzling Gleam threat that can KO Garchomp from 45%. Gyarados is immune to Earthquake but burned, limiting its physical damage. Rock Slide doesn't guarantee KO on either target. reflections.summary: Won effectively 3v4 after Mega Gengar fainted T1 on a Focus Blast miss — Shadow Tag trapped nothing. Gyarados chipped Garchomp to 17% via two Dragon Dances and Waterfall despite being burned T7. Aegislash's King's Shield reverted it to Shield forme, letting it survive Garchomp's Earthquake T12 and KO the 17% Garchomp with Close Combat. Klefki's Reflect was essential for physical damage mitigation. The final crit was unnecessary at that HP.
reflections.adjustment: Reassess the Mega Gengar bring — it contributed zero value and the team won without it. If Gengar returns, avoid high-variance Focus Blast early and only lead it where Shadow Tag guarantees a key trap. Also prepare for Scarf Rotom-W (unseen G1) as a Gyarados answer in G2-3, and exploit the opponent's frequent Protect reads with double-attack lines.
reflections.notebook: Opp tendencies: high Protect frequency — favors Protect reads; Garchomp defaults to Earthquake. Opp brought Garchomp/Arcanine/Tinkaton/Archaludon G1; Rotom-W (Scarf) and Blaziken (Sash, Speed Boost) unseen — likely adjustments for G2-3. Gyarados +1 Spe (219) outspeeds all opp mons including Scarf Rotom-W. Watch Scarf Rotom-W as Gyarados counter. Aegislash King's Shield reverts to Shield forme — survives Garchomp EQ in Shield forme; Blade forme OHKO'd (122-212%). Burned Gyarados needs +2 Atk to offset burn; +1 burned Waterfall does 15-33% to Garchomp. Life Orb + Rough Skin contact KOs Gyarados at low HP. Reflect critical for Aegislash survival vs physical hits. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag contributed nothing G1 (fainted T1 Focus Blast miss) — reassess Mega choice; if Gengar returns, lead only where Shadow Tag guarantees a key trap. Consider double-attack lines to punish Protect stalls. Prepare for Speed Boost Blaziken and Scarf Volt Switch if opp adjusts.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team-preview plan lacked a Mega to break the opponent's physical core and relied on Garchomp as the closer. Garchomp was completely walled by Gyarados (immune to Earthquake) and Aegislash (physically bulky behind Klefki's Reflect), failing to secure the final KO and allowing Aegislash to win with a critical Close Combat.
reflections.adjustment: In team preview, bring a Mega or a dedicated special attacker like Archaludon over physical attackers to bypass Gyarados's Ground immunity and Klefki's Reflect, ensuring reliable damage against their physical walls.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Klefki to set Reflect early, enabling Gyarados and Aegislash to wall physical attacks. Gyarados runs Life Orb Jolly with Dragon Dance and completely walls Ground-type moves. Aegislash runs Brave Leftovers with King's Shield and Close Combat, relying on physical bulk and Reflect to survive. Opponent's back includes Rotom-Heat (Expert Belt) and Ditto (Choice Scarf). Future plan: Lead with special attackers or a Mega to ignore Reflect and hit Gyarados/Aegislash reliably. Avoid bringing physical Ground-types as the primary win condition against this core.
